title: there is / there are and where things are
tagline: Say what's in a room, a bag or a town — and exactly where it is.
exam: Listening Part 1 — a picture and five short conversations
why: You use there is and there are all the time — to describe your room, your town or a picture. Prepositions of place (in, on, under, next to…) tell your listener exactly where something is. That's exactly what Listening Part 1 tests: spotting the right picture from small details.

hook.text: Nadia has a new bedroom. "There's a big window next to my bed, and there are two shelves above my desk. Is there a mirror?" "No," says Sofia, "but there's one in the hall!"
hook.ask: Find all the times the story says there is or there are. Which one is for one thing, and which is for more than one?

diagrams.title: Build the sentence with there is / there are
diagrams.caption: There's (there is) for one thing, there are for two or more. In a question, is/are jumps straight after there.

branches.label: between
items: between the sofa and the TV

diagrams.title: How to ask Is there…?

steps.label: Add the place and the question mark
steps.ex: Is there a mirror in your room?

diagrams.caption: Use Is there…? for one thing and Are there any…? for more than one.

head: One thing
More than one
rows: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

examples.text: There's a big window next to my bed.
examples.note: There's = there is, for one thing

examples.text: There is a park near my house.

examples.note: milk is uncountable, so it takes is

use.point: There are — two or more things

examples.text: There are two shelves above my desk.
There are some books on the floor.
examples.note: some + plural noun in a positive sentence

examples.text: There aren't any posters on the wall.
examples.note: any in negatives with plural nouns

use.point: Questions and short answers with any

examples.text: Is there a mirror in your room?
examples.note: is there + a for one thing

examples.text: Are there any shops near the school?
examples.note: are there + any for more than one

examples.text: Is there a park near here? — Yes, there is.
The mirror is next to the door.
examples.note: next to = at the side of

examples.text: The school is between the park and the shop.
examples.note: between = with one thing on each side
opposite = facing, on the other side

watch_out.wrong: Is a book on the table.
watch_out.right: Is there a book on the table?
watch_out.why: You need the word there in the question — is alone doesn't mean 'is there'.
A plural noun needs are, not is.

watch_out.wrong: There are a park near my house.
watch_out.right: There is a park near my house.
watch_out.why: A/an is singular, so use is, not are.
A singular noun with a/an takes isn't, not aren't.

watch_out.wrong: The cat is in front the sofa.
watch_out.right: The cat is in front of the sofa.
watch_out.why: In front of needs the little word of — it never stands alone.

watch_out.wrong: There's many people at the party.
watch_out.right: There are a lot of people at the party.
watch_out.why: A plural noun needs are, and a lot of sounds more natural than many in a positive statement.

l1.es: Hay un libro en la mesa.
l1.wrong: Is a book on the table.
l1.why: Spanish hay has no subject; English always needs there before is/are.

l1.es: Hay dos gatos en el jardín.
l1.wrong: There is two cats in the garden.
l1.right: There are two cats in the garden.
l1.why: Plural noun (two cats) needs are, not is.

l1.es: El gato está debajo de la mesa.
l1.wrong: The cat is down the table.
l1.why: Debajo de translates to under, not down.

l1.es: La tienda está enfrente del colegio.
l1.wrong: The shop is enfront the school.
l1.why: The English word is opposite, and it needs no of after it.

l1.es: No hay leche en la nevera.
l1.why: Milk is uncountable — no a/an, and any in negatives.

remember.trick: There's = one. There are = two or more!
remember.tip: Listen for the S: There's = one thing. No S: There are = two or more things.

dialogue.title: Nadia's new room
dialogue.context: Nadia has just moved to a new house in Lima. Sofia comes to see her bedroom for the first time.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Wow, Nadia! Is there a balcony in your room?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: No, there isn't, but there's a big window next to my bed.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Nice! Are there any posters on the wall?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Not yet. There are two shelves above my desk, though.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: It's next to the door, opposite my bed.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: That's my old toy box. There's a lot of stuff in it!

items.sentence: ___ a park near your house?
items.why: Is there + a + singular noun, for a question about one thing.

items.sentence: ___ some apples in the bag.
items.why: apples is plural, and this is a statement, so use There are.

items.sentence: ___ any milk in the fridge?
items.why: milk is uncountable, so it takes is, even with any.

items.sentence: There ___ a mirror in the hall.
There ___ any chairs in the room.
items.why: chairs is plural, so the negative is aren't.

items.sentence: The cat is ___ the table.
The bank is ___ the market.
items.why: opposite = facing, on the other side.

items.sentence: ___ two shelves above my desk.
items.why: two shelves is plural, and this is a statement, so use There are.

can_do: I can say what's in a room, a bag or a town with there is and there are.
I can ask Is there…? and Are there any…? and answer them.
I can use in, on, under, next to, between and opposite to say exactly where something is.
summary: There's (there is) for one thing; there are for two or more.
Questions: Is there…? / Are there any…? — is/are comes straight after there.
Prepositions of place say exactly where: in, on, under, next to, between, opposite, near.
Use a/an or some in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions.
